description: Training data quality improvements in notebooks/CommitBench_filter.ipynb: add deduplication (by diff+message hash), add class rebalancing (cap fix at ~20% of total per split), and add placeholder cleaning to training messages (apply clean_message logic inline). These changes address the known model bias and data leakage issues identified in results.md and plan.md. Independent of FEAT-001.
steps: Step 1 — Read the full notebooks/CommitBench_filter.ipynb to understand the exact cell structure and where the config section ends and the build_example/filter loop begins.

Step 2 — Add RANDOM_SEED = 42 constant to the config cell (after MAX_FILES_PER_DIFF). This constant is referenced in the eval notebook's shuffle call; making it explicit here is the right place to document reproducibility intent.

Step 3 — Add deduplication: add 'seen_hashes: set[str] = set()' before the per-split loop. In build_example(), after all validity checks, compute h = hashlib.sha256((truncated + message).encode()).hexdigest()[:16]; if h in seen_hashes: return None; seen_hashes.add(h). Note: seen_hashes must be reset between splits to avoid cross-split deduplication (each split is filtered independently and dedup should be within-split only). Add 'import hashlib' to the imports cell. Track and print 'dedup_removed' count per split.

Step 4 — Add class rebalancing: add MAX_PER_TYPE: dict[str, int] = {'fix': 12000} to the config cell (only fix is capped; all other types are uncapped). Add type_counts: dict[str, int] = {} before the per-split write loop. In build_example() or in the write loop, extract the commit type via the same CONVENTIONAL_PREFIX regex (already defined in the notebook), and skip if type_counts.get(type, 0) >= MAX_PER_TYPE.get(type, float('inf')). Print per-type counts at end of each split. Note: MAX_PER_TYPE only caps on train split — validation and test should be left uncapped for representative evaluation. Add logic to skip capping for split_name != 'train'.

Step 5 — Add placeholder cleaning to training messages: inline the same regex logic as clean_message() from src/commit_model/postprocess.py into a helper function clean_training_message(message: str) -> str at the top of the config cell. Apply it to the message in build_example() AFTER the CONVENTIONAL_PREFIX and low-content checks (so cleaned messages still pass the original format check). The function should strip <I>, <URL>, <EMAIL>, <HASH> placeholders and the pull-request reference patterns exactly as clean_message() does, but do NOT include the lowercase-first-word logic (that is inference-time cosmetic only). Keep the message's prefix (feat:, fix:, etc.) intact. If cleaning results in an empty description (e.g. 'fix: (#<I>)' becomes 'fix: '), reject the example (return None from build_example). Print a 'placeholder_cleaned' counter per split.

Step 6 — Verify the output JSONL schema is unchanged: each output line must still be {"diff": str, "message": str} with no additional fields. Add an assertion in the sanity-check cell at the end of the notebook.
acceptance_criteria: notebooks/CommitBench_filter.ipynb is valid JSON (can be parsed by json.load)
The notebook's Python source cells are syntactically valid Python (ast.parse passes on extracted source)
The output schema per example remains {"diff": str, "message": str} — no added fields
MAX_PER_TYPE dict is present in the config cell
RANDOM_SEED = 42 is present in the config cell
clean_training_message function is defined and applied in build_example
hashlib is imported and seen_hashes dedup logic is present
Class rebalancing only applies to the 'train' split (validation and test are uncapped)
